punchline: Couples argued in a laboratory, and after the hostile arguments their blood showed lower immune markers.
thirty_sec: Psychologist Janice Kiecolt-Glaser had married couples talk through a disagreement and gave them a blood test. After hostile conversations, their immune measures were lower than after calmer ones. Gabor Maté uses the study to show that mind and body are not separate systems. It was a short-term difference, not proof that arguing makes you ill.
